title: Determination of the VIS/NIR-LSF (light protection factor) for dark skin types using the DRS method and reference measurements analogous to ISO24444
summary: The sun protection factor of sunscreens is currently only tested on skin types I to III in a sun simulator. The test subjects are exposed to minimal doses of erythema. People with darker skin do not receive sufficient sun protection. This is a problem because melanomas are often recognised too late. We need to find a way to measure the sun protection factor in darker skin types. This study is investigating how this can be done using LED technology. The aim is to develop a device that can measure the SPF of cream formulations for all skin types (I to VI) in the visible (VIS/NIR) spectral range without causing artificial sunburn.
conditions: Healthy volunteers with a skin type of I to VI are examined in this study.

interventions.name: Application of cream formulations to the back and investigation of the protective effect in the VIS/NIR range for skin types IV to VI using the DRS measurement method  (non-invasive)

Reference measurement: Verification of the protective effect of cream formulations on the back and investigation of the protective effect in the VIS/NIR range for skin types I to III using the DRS measurement method  (non-invasive)

Reference measurement: Verification of the protective effect of cream formulations on the back, and investigation of the protective effect in the VIS/NIR range for skin types IV to VI by determining the carotenoid concentration in skin with/without cream application (non-invasive)

Reference measurement: Verification of the protective effect of cream formulations on the inner forearm, and investigation of the protective effect in the VIS/NIR range for skin types IV to VI by measuring radical production in the skin without/with cream application (non-invasive)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Skin-healthy subjects older than 18 years, younger than 70 years 
- have ITA° values of at least 28 for skin types I-III  
- have ITA° values of << 28 for skin type IV-VI  
- are informed about the objectives of the study and the nature of the examinations 
- have given written informed consent to participate
Exclusion criteria:
- Minors or persons older than 70 years 
- Pregnant and breastfeeding women 
- Subjects under medication with photosensitising potential  
- Subjects with known skin diseases 
- Subjects who have previously reacted abnormally to UV radiation 
- Subjects with spots, blemishes or pigmentation on the test area that affect the results (ITA value variation ≤ 5%)
- Test subjects with sun damage in the test area (e.g. severe skin wrinkling and diffuse pigmentation) 
- Test subjects with known allergies and intolerance reactions to cosmetics  
- Subjects who have heavy hair growth on the test area on the day of the test (hair may be shaved up to 3 days before the day of the test or cut on the day of the measurement) 
- Persons who have not given their informed consent in writing
- Persons who are unable to make decisions on their own responsibility
